source.publication: 2025 Oklahoma Resident Individual Income Tax Forms and Instructions (Form 511 packet)
source.section: Form 511 lines 1-14 and 18 (PDF pages 42-43); select line instructions (PDF pages 9-10); standard deduction line 10 (PDF page 10); exemptions line 11 and the Regular exemption terms (PDF pages 8 and 10); Tax Table (PDF pages 27-38); Special exemption and Sixty-five or older (PDF page 9)

worked: Federal AGI = wages (you) 40,000.00 = 40,000.00. Federal taxable income = 40,000.00 - standard deduction 33,100.00 (31,500.00 + 1 x 1,600.00 for 65 or older) = 6,900.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Oklahoma starts from federal AGI). Form 511: line 1 federal AGI 40,000.00; line 2 subtractions 0.00; line 3 = 40,000.00 - 0.00 = 40,000.00; line 4 out-of-state income 0.00; line 5 40,000.00; line 6 additions 0.00; line 7 Oklahoma AGI 40,000.00; line 8 adjustments 0.00; line 9 40,000.00; line 10 standard deduction (qualifying surviving spouse) 12,700.00; line 11 exemptions: 1 Regular + 0 Special = 1 x 1,000.00 = 1,000.00 (line 1 is over every limit the booklet prints, so no Special exemption whichever limit a qualifying surviving spouse would have); line 12 = 12,700.00 + 1,000.00 = 13,700.00; line 13 taxable income = 40,000.00 - 13,700.00 = 26,300.00; line 14 tax (the projection's brackets as numbers; the booklet prints only a table and worksheets): 0.25% x 2,000.00 = 5.0000 + 0.75% x 3,000.00 = 22.5000 + 1.75% x 2,500.00 = 43.7500 + 2.75% x 2,300.00 = 63.2500 + 3.75% x 4,600.00 = 172.5000 + 4.75% x 11,900.00 = 565.2500; total 872.2500 = 872.25. Line 13 is under 100,000, so the form reads the tax table: row 26,300-26,350, column 'Married filing joint or head of household', PDF page 30, gives 873; expected keeps the schedule figure. Lines 15-17 credits 0.00; line 18 income tax 872.25. Page 9 prints no limit for this status. Line 1 is 40,000.00, over all four printed limits, so no Special exemption whether this filer is barred or takes the joint limit. No dependents in the inputs; the form would add 1,000.00 for each.
accepted_approximations: The brackets are derived from the printed tax table and the 100,000-and-over worksheets; the booklet prints no schedule. Below 100,000 tax is figured on the exact income, where the booklet taxes each 50-dollar row at its midpoint and rounds. At 100,000 and over the single and separate worksheet starts from 4,562 where the schedule gives 4,561.50.

The age 65 exemption has no printed limit for a qualifying surviving spouse: the four returns listed are single, joint, separate and head of household, and the threshold here holds only those. The booklet does not say whether that filer may claim it.
The blind and dependent exemptions and the credits are left out (not_modelled).
